tools.name: list_monitors
tools.description: Requires the read scope or higher. Lists every monitor in the project with id, name, slug, status and ping_url. tag narrows the list to monitors carrying one tag.

tag.description: Optional tag to filter by, e.g. 'agent:claude'. Only monitors with this tag are returned.

tools.name: discover_monitors_reconcile
tools.description: Requires the write scope or higher. Turns a scan of a repository or host (`sources`, every scheduled job found) into monitors. Creates one monitor per source not already monitored; never deletes, pauses or edits existing monitors, so a scheduled re-run is safe drift detection. Returns `created`, `existing` (unmodified, hand-tuned values intact) and `orphaned` (source not in this scan; still running and alerting). Each created monitor can page a person; this endpoint has no delete path. source_kind plus source_ref is the diff key, so source_ref has to stay stable: a changed ref creates a duplicate; a crontab ref names the file and the command, so each line is its own source. Kinds: 'crontab' (crontab -l, /etc/cron.d/*, /etc/crontab), 'github-actions' (on.schedule.cron), 'k8s-cronjob' (spec.schedule), 'systemd-timer' (OnCalendar=). A source without schedule_cron becomes on-demand. crontab and systemd-timer fire in the host's local time (`timedatectl show -p Timezone --value` or `readlink /etc/localtime` prints it); github-actions and k8s-cronjob in UTC. A stated tz is stored as given: the API cannot tell a guessed 'UTC' from one read from the host. list_monitors shows each source.

sources.description: The full scan as a JSON array string, e.g. '[{"source_kind":"crontab","source_ref":"/etc/cron.d/backup:/usr/local/bin/backup.sh","schedule_cron":"0 3 * * *","tz":"Europe/Berlin"}]'. Fields: source_kind, source_ref (required), name (default source_ref), schedule_cron (5-field, when one was read), tz (IANA zone the cron fires in; required on a crontab or systemd-timer entry with schedule_cron), suggested_expect_every_s (overrides the silence floor). An omitted source is reported orphaned; '[]' orphans every discovered monitor, deleting none. At most 1000 entries; a repeated source_kind/source_ref pair is rejected. The 100-monitor cap covers the whole batch; one invalid entry rejects it all.

tools.name: create_monitor
tools.description: Requires the write scope or higher. Creates a monitor, or updates the existing one when slug matches (an upsert; the result says 'updated'). Heartbeat and ci monitors take schedule_kind: 'simple' with period_s, 'cron' with cron_expr, or 'on_demand' with neither.

name.description: Human-readable monitor name, e.g. 'Daily backup job'.

agent_id.description: Attaches the monitor to a registered agent, by the agent's id or slug (register_agent returns both).

schedule_kind.description: 'simple' (with period_s), 'cron' (with cron_expr) or 'on_demand' (neither). 'on_demand' fits irregular invocation.

cron_expr.description: 5-field cron expression, e.g. '0 3 * * *'. Required when schedule_kind='cron'.

period_s.description: Ping interval in seconds. Required when schedule_kind='simple'.

tz.description: IANA timezone for cron evaluation. Defaults to UTC.

expect_every_s.description: Silence floor in seconds: a 'silence' incident opens when no ping of any kind arrives within this window. Unset (default): no floor. Range 60-31536000.

tools.name: update_monitor
tools.description: Requires the write scope or higher. Updates a monitor by UUID with merge-patch semantics: supplied fields change, omitted fields keep their stored value.

expect_every_s.description: Silence floor in seconds. Omitted: unchanged; 0 clears it and turns the silence floor off.

tools.name: register_agent
tools.description: Requires the write scope or higher. Registers an autonomous agent in the project's agent registry and returns its id, slug and wire-up steps. One agent stands for one autonomous worker, which can own many monitors: create_monitor and update_monitor attach a monitor through agent_id (the id or the slug).

name.description: Human-readable agent name, e.g. 'Deploy Bot'. Used to derive the agent's slug.

description.description: Optional free-text description of what this agent does. Omitted: none.

tools.name: get_ping_instructions
tools.description: Requires the read scope or higher. Returns what a monitor needs in order to report: its ping URLs, copy-paste snippets (curl_success, curl_start, curl_fail, curl_step, run_example) and three reporting mechanisms, for wiring up a new monitor. `reporting_options` holds the rule for choosing between them: `how_to` is the manual protocol and works in any agent with no prerequisite (with expect_every_s, a lapse opens an incident); `hook_install` is a one-time install that automates the same protocol through hooks and alone sends every state, blocked and note included; it is returned only when `tool` is set (claude-code, codex or antigravity), otherwise `hook_install_note` says so; `run_wrapper` puts `lastping run` before a launched command (cron job, CI step, script) and reports start, success, fail and cancel.

tool.description: Which tool's install `hook_install` carries: claude-code, codex or antigravity. `hook_install` is returned only when this is set. Everything else in the result is the same.

tools.name: list_destinations
tools.description: Requires the read scope or higher. Lists the project's notification destinations (channels) of every kind (webhook, telegram, discord, slack, ntfy, pushover, msteams, googlechat, email). Their ids are what set_route takes.
